title: How the Log Streaming Service reaches a SIEM

prose.text: LSS forwards ZPA logs through an App Connector, so the path, the order of deployment and the reach of the receiver follow from that.

prose.label: Which connector group carries the stream.
Log Connector groups.
prose.text: {{log-connector-groups}} {{log-connector-group-details}} How a Log Connector relates to an App Connector, and whether receivers use Log Connector groups or the App Connector groups above, is open {{gap:log-connector}}.

prose.label: Business Continuity Event log.
prose.text: The field table and example record of the Business Continuity Event log disagree, a divergence recorded in [[zpa.log-receivers.log-types]].
Capacity of a receiver and reaching an internet-exposed SIEM are not sourced {{gap:capacity-limits}} {{gap:internet-exposed-receiver}}.

checks.do: That the App Connector group named on the receiver exists and has deployed, connected connectors.
That the SIEM address and port are reachable from the network the App Connector sits in, not from the internet or the cloud.
Whether the receiver's address overlaps an application segment whose Bypass setting changes what a user device can reach.
Whether more than one connector group points at the same stream, which sends the log once per group.

purpose.statement: LSS lets an organization create log receivers that receive information about App Connectors and users in Private Access; the help lists forwarding diagnostics and status logs to a SIEM and storing logs longer than the cloud retention period among its benefits.

quotes: The Log Streaming Service (LSS) provides a better understanding of the information coming from the Private Access (ZPA) service by allowing you to create log receivers that receive information about App Connectors and users.
Forward your diagnostics and status logs to a SIEM.
Store logs for longer than the cloud retention period.

two-components.statement: LSS is deployed using two components, a log receiver and an App Connector: LSS resides in the Zero Trust Exchange and starts a log stream through a Public Service Edge, and the App Connector in the company's environment receives the stream and forwards it to the log receiver.

quotes: LSS is deployed using two components: a log receiver and an App Connector.
LSS resides in the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) and initiates a log stream through a Public Service Edge for Private Access.
The App Connector resides in your company's enterprise environment. It receives the log stream and then forwards it to a log receiver.

tcp-port.statement: A receiver is addressed by a domain name or IP address and a TCP port, the port on which the log receiver listens for incoming log streams.

quotes: Domain Name or IP Address: The domain name or IP address for the receiver.
TCP Port: The TCP port that the log receiver is listening on for incoming log streams.

not-nss.statement: LSS captures log data about App Connectors and users in Private Access, while the Nanolog Streaming Service resides in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and streams traffic logs from the Zscaler Nanolog to a SIEM.

quotes: While the LSS is used to capture log data about App Connectors and users in Private Access using a log receiver, the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) resides in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and allows streaming of traffic logs from the Zscaler Nanolog to your SIEM.

third-party-siem.statement: Zscaler supports third-party SIEM integrations for LSS and points to its Private Access and Splunk Deployment Guide and Zscaler and Splunk Deployment Guide.

quotes: Zscaler supports third-party SIEM integrations for the LSS. To learn more, see the Private Access and Splunk Deployment Guide and Zscaler and Splunk Deployment Guide.

connectors-first.statement: App Connectors must be deployed before a log receiver is configured.

quotes: Your App Connectors must be deployed prior to configuring a log receiver.
Your App Connectors must be deployed prior to configuring a log receiver.

receiver-reachable-from-connector.statement: Because the App Connector forwards the stream to the receiver, the receiver's address and port must be reachable from the App Connector's network.
receiver-reachable-from-connector.conditions: Inference from the documented path (cloud to connector to receiver); the help does not state a reachability requirement in these words.

closest-group.statement: Logs go to the App Connector group that is geographically closest to the LSS instance, and transmission switches to App Connectors in another location when the connectors of the previously selected group are unavailable.

quotes: Logs go to the App Connector group that is geographically closest to the instance of the Log Streaming Service (LSS).
In the event that the App Connectors in a previously selected App Connector group are not available, then log transmission switches to App Connectors in another location.

duplicate-per-group.statement: If each App Connector group points to a different log receiver and is configured for the exact same LSS, the same log is sent to an App Connector in each group.

quotes: If each App Connector group points to a different log receiver and is configured for the exact same LSS, then the same log is sent to an App Connector in each App Connector group.

internal-segment.statement: When a log receiver is created, the service also creates an internal application segment with the receiver's FQDN or IP address, and if that address overlaps an application segment, the segment's Bypass setting takes precedence, so a bypassed address on a trusted network is unreachable from the user's device.

quotes: If the FQDN or IP address of the log receiver overlaps with or is the same as the wildcard domain or IP subnet defined in an application segment, the Bypass setting configured for the application segment takes precedence.
As a result, if the FQDN or IP address is bypassed for a user on a trusted network, the user's device cannot communicate with the log receiver.
When creating a log receiver, the Zscaler service also creates an internal application segment with the same FQDN or IP address.

log-connector-groups.statement: The Log Connector Groups page is under Data Explorer > Log Streaming > Private Log Streaming > Log Connector Groups. Each Log Connector is mapped to one Log Connector group, a log type is then mapped to one or multiple Log Connector groups for log forwarding, and the Log Connector must be up and running for the group to be active.

quotes: Each Log Connector is mapped to one Log Connector group. A log type is then mapped to one or multiple Log Connector groups for log forwarding. Ensure that your Log Connector is up and running for the Log Connector group to be active.
Data Explorer > Log Streaming > Private Log Streaming > Log Connector Groups

log-connector-group-details.statement: A Log Connector group's details include its Location, the Enrollment Certificate its Log Connectors use for enrollment, a DNS Resolution Option, Disaster Recovery, Disable AppProtection and Privileged Remote Access flags, a Version Profile for the Log Connector build, the next periodic software update, Network Settings (network parameters such as DNS, routing, proxy servers and time services), and the numbers of enrolled App Connectors and provisioning keys associated with the group.

quotes: Location: The location where the Log Connector group, which the Log Connector belongs to, is set up.
Enrollment Certificate: The certificate the Log Connector uses for enrollment.
DNS Resolution Option: Specifies how the Log Connectors in the group resolve DNS queries.
Disaster Recovery: Indicates whether Disaster Recovery is enabled or disabled.
Disable AppProtection: Indicates whether AppProtection is enabled or disabled.
Privileged Remote Access: Indicates whether Privileged Remote Access (PRA) is enabled or disabled.
Version Profile: The profile used to specify a Log Connector build for the group.
Next Periodic Software Update is on: The date and time of the next periodic software update for all of the Log Connectors within the group.
Network Settings: Displays network parameters for the Log Connector group such as DNS, routing, proxy servers, and time services.
App Connectors: The number of enrolled App Connectors associated with this group.
Provisioning Keys: The number of enrolled provisioning keys associated with this group.

log-connector.title: What a Log Connector is and how its groups relate to App Connector groups
log-connector.detail: The Log Connector Groups page does not say how a Log Connector relates to an App Connector (the group drawer counts App Connectors and provisioning keys), whether log receivers in the Data Explorer view use Log Connector groups instead of the App Connector groups described in this subject, or why its benefits list says to group Log Connectors to ensure logs are streamed to an identity provider.

internet-exposed-receiver.title: A receiver exposed to the internet and Splunk transports
internet-exposed-receiver.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Internet-exposed SIEM endpoints work if the App Connector has outbound internet access. Splunk (HTTP Event Collector or raw TCP)." The stream is addressed by host and TCP port (tcp-port) and the help names the Splunk deployment guides (third-party-siem); no captured source says that an internet-exposed endpoint works or that Splunk HTTP Event Collector is a supported transport.

capacity-limits.title: Receiver throughput and capacity
capacity-limits.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Log receiver capacity limits are determined by the App Connector's throughput and network path, not by a Zscaler-side quota. The help doc does not publish explicit per-receiver throughput limits. Capacity is constrained by App Connector CPU/network and the log receiver's ingestion capacity. High-volume tenants may need to distribute log types across multiple receivers or increase App Connector resources." No captured source states a throughput limit or quota for a receiver, or what constrains it. The only published limit near receivers is 1,000 application segments per Log Receiver Policy rule (see zpa.log-receivers.filtering).
